choices: The new clerk is not only careful but also works fast.
The new clerk is not only careful but also fast.
The new clerk not only is careful but also fast.
The new clerk is not only careful but also she is fast.
answer: The new clerk is not only careful but also fast.
hints: "Not only … but also" is a pair. What comes after "not only" must match what comes after "but also".
In each choice, find the words right after "not only" and the words right after "but also". Are they the same kind of word?
If "not only" is followed by a describing word (like "careful"), "but also" must be followed by a describing word too. Check each choice.

solution.methodName: Line up the parts, then match the forms

steps.action: In each choice, find what follows "not only" and what follows "but also".
First choice: "careful" (a describing word) against "works fast" (an action). They do not match. Wrong.
Second choice: "careful" against "fast". Both are describing words, so they match. Correct.
steps.why: A describing word (an adjective) tells what a person or thing is like: careful, fast, new.

steps.action: Third choice: "is careful" against "fast". The first half has a verb; the second does not. Wrong.
Fourth choice: "careful" against "she is fast", a full sentence. They do not match. Wrong.
The answer is "The new clerk is not only careful but also fast."

trapNotes.The new clerk is not only careful but al: "Works fast" says the same idea, so it sounds fine. But it is an action, while "careful" is a describing word. The two halves do not match.
trapNotes.The new clerk not only is careful but al: This moves "is" after "not only", so the first half becomes "is careful" while the second half is only "fast".
trapNotes.The new clerk is not only careful but al: Adding "she is" makes the second half a full sentence, while the first half is one word, "careful".
